Entry Books and Scribes of Oldtown The Citadel of Oldtown, the Order, and the Great Merchants made books, maps, parchment, and ink a negotiable commodity. Bachelors see knowledge as a duty, scribes see it as a craft, and nobles use their collections of books to prove their taste; but most people have little idea of ​​the power of these volumes. Any break in the place of origin, checkpoints, shipping schedules, debts and protection fees will immediately make the nobles in the distance feel the changes in price and power.

Entry Books and Scribes of Oldtown The Citadel of Oldtown, the Order, and the Great Merchants made books, maps, parchment, and ink a negotiable commodity. Bachelors see knowledge as a duty, scribes see it as a craft, and nobles use their collections of books to prove their taste; but most people have little idea of ​​the power of these volumes. They may not necessarily understand ledgers, but they know the true weight of a bag of salt and a nail on the road.

Entry Books and Scribes of Oldtown The Citadel of Oldtown, the Order, and the Great Merchants made books, maps, parchment, and ink a negotiable commodity. Bachelors see knowledge as a duty, scribes see it as a craft, and nobles use their collections of books to prove their taste; but most people have little idea of ​​the power of these volumes. Some people turn raw materials into tools, cloth and medicine, others set festivals and taboos for exchange; wealth is piled up by many hands, and rarely belongs to just one name.

Bachelors see knowledge as a duty, scribes see it as a craft, and nobles use their collections of books to prove their taste; but most people have little idea of ​​the power of these volumes. If prices rise but wages do not, prosperity in distant places will only become thinner bread; if roads are safe, even small villages can get a little spring from trade.
